page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc5s.24xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal server powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a 1:2 compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per core. The underlying infrastructure utilizes KVM to supply dedicated core allocation without multi-tenant hypervisor resource contention.

Networking performance is anchored by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing high-throughput interconnectivity for distributed environments. The server includes no bundled local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external block storage for data persistence and root volumes. There are no discrete hardware graphics processors and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included in the base hardware specification.

The dense 96-core footprint paired with a modest 192.0 GB memory capacity offers high compute efficiency for CPU-limited processing. The hardware profile is appropriate for workloads such as batch compute processing, large software build pipelines, distributed simulation tasks, and high-concurrency stateless web services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc5s.24xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The server configuration features 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Operating on a KVM hypervisor foundation with dedicated CPU allocation, it avoids noisy-neighbor contention. The platform is provisioned with a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for high-speed node communication. Local storage is not integrated into this profile, requiring external network-attached volumes for all storage needs, and the server includes zero GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its high core density and balanced compute profile, this bare-metal server is structured for compute-heavy workloads, including large-scale software compilation, distributed batch processing, and continuous integration clusters.
